title: U.S. House · Texas's 1st District
area: East Texas, including Tyler, Texarkana, Longview, and Marshall

context.text: Incumbent Nathaniel Moran (R) ran unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Yolanda Prince won a May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff against Dax Alexander, 72.3% to 27.7%.

candidates.name: Nathaniel Moran

summary.text: Nathaniel Moran is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 1st Congressional District, an attorney and former Tyler City Council member.

background.text: Born in Whitehouse, Texas; graduated from Whitehouse High School and earned a law degree from Texas Tech University.
Worked as an attorney and partner with the law firm Ramey & Flock, P.C. before serving on the Tyler City Council.

record.text: Serves on the U.S. House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, among other committee assignments, in the 2025–2026 Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Moran's official site lists issue pages (Economy, Education, Election Integrity, Pro-Life, Energy, Veterans, Border Security) but the content loads via JavaScript and was not accessible to extract specific position statements or quotes in this research pass.

candidates.name: Yolanda Prince
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff

summary.text: Yolanda Prince is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 1st Congressional District, a university project manager.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Stephen F. Austin University and a graduate degree from the University of Texas at Arlington.
Career experience includes working as a university project manager.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, candidate questionnaire, or public policy statements found for Prince; only basic biographical facts from Ballotpedia are documented.
